record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: For the conflict-zone memory system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i + γ_i∇·(u_i∇k_i g,R), ∂_t k_i = u_i Σ_j=1^n ρ_ij u_j − (μ + βu_i)k_i, in what sense do solutions exist on a bounded domain with a top-hat detection function when the boundary conditions are zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. In what sense do solutions exist solving the time-dependent problem (2.13) subject to zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions with a top-hat detection in a bounded domain?

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $n\ge 2$ be an integer. For $i=1,\dots,n$, let $d_i>0$, $\gamma_i\in\mathbb{R}$, $\mu>0$, $ eta\ge 0$, and let $(ho_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ be a given matrix of nonnegative real numbers. For a parameter $R>0$, define the top-hat detection kernel
$$\eta_R(x) =  rac{1}{|B_R(0)|}\,\mathbf{1}_{B_R(0)}(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^N,$$
and for a function $f:\Omega	o\mathbb{R}$ (extended by $0$ outside $\Omega$) the nonlocal gradient detection
$$
abla f|_{g,R}(x) = (\eta_R \ast 
abla f)(x).$$
Consider the coupled system, for unknowns $u_i,k_i:\Omega	imes(0,T)	o\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$,
$$\partial_t u_i = d_i\,\Delta u_i + \gamma_i\,
abla\!\cdot\! igl(u_i\,
abla k_i|_{g,R} igr),$$
$$\partial_t k_i = u_i\sum_{j=1}^n ho_{ij} u_j \;-\;(\mu+ eta u_i)\,k_i,$$
for $i=1,\dots,n$, equipped with nonnegative initial data $u_i(\cdot,0)=u_{i,0}$, $k_i(\cdot,0)=k_{i,0}$, and one of the following boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega$:
(a) zero-flux: $d_i\,\partial_
u u_i + \gamma_i\,u_i\,(
abla k_i|_{g,R})\!\cdot\!
u = 0$;
(b) homogeneous Neumann: $\partial_
u u_i = 0$;
(c) homogeneous Dirichlet: $u_i = 0$.

Determine in what functional-analytic sense (e.g., classical, strong, weak, or measure-valued) solutions to this initial-boundary value problem exist, and establish a corresponding well-posedness theory (existence, uniqueness, regularity, and nonnegativity) under each of the three boundary conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on PDE models of animal movement with nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping. A targeted web search did not turn up any subsequent work establishing a well-posedness theory for this conflict-zone memory system with top-hat detection on bounded domains under the listed boundary conditions, so the problem appears to remain open.
